context: seed: JSON files of this world open with a byte order mark that a strict parser refuses (suite/families/curriculum.py:232); every clothing of the bom lesson reads one .json file through the file tool and returns fields from it, unbudgeted
counterfactual: The overshoot is passing the raw text to a strict parser — the naive policy at suite/families/conventions.py:67 and suite/families/curriculum.py:226 — when the files are written with the mark at suite/families/curriculum.py:232; the other overshoot is stripping leading bytes from a file that is not JSON.
decision: A JSON file read through the file tool may open with a byte order mark (U+FEFF) that a strict parser refuses. Strip it before parsing: take the file text, drop a leading `\ufeff`, then parse as JSON (`json.loads(text.lstrip('\ufeff'))`, or decode the bytes as `utf-8-sig`). Then read the named keys and count the named list. Write any requested output file as plain JSON with no byte order mark, and return the object the prompt names with its keys exactly as asked.

residue: which keys and which list the prompt names is read off the prompt

not_this: a CSV or plain text file read through the shell
an HTTP response body, which carries no byte order mark
a parse failure whose cause is not a leading byte order mark — a truncated or malformed file is a different fault
